facts.fact: The APD's own FAQ page tells citizens to lodge complaints about breaches of the data protection law with the APD and says it assesses transfer adequacy case by case under art. 33 of Lei 22/11; the page is undated, so the published date is used.
The APD, headed by Executive Director Amaro Santos Figueiredo, held a training session for journalists in Luanda with the IFC on private credit information centres.

The APD's President of the Board, Maria das Dores Pinto, signed a cooperation memorandum with Brazil's ANPD at the Global Privacy Assembly in Seoul; the page is undated and the date is inferred from the event.

The APD's President signed Circular 02/APD/2024 requiring public and private entities to notify it of personal data breaches, citing its mandate under art. 44 of Lei 22/11 and Presidential Decree 214/16 on its organic statute.
CAZOS says the Agência de Protecção de Dados (APD), created by Presidential Decree 214/16, exists, supervises and has sanctioning powers.
Portal de TI quotes Njunjulo António, legal director of Angola's Agência de Protecção de Dados (APD), describing the agency's inspection and audit work.

facts.fact: Expansao says the Agencia de Proteccao de Dados was created in October 2016 by Presidential Decree 214/16 and has operated effectively since October 2019.
Expansao reports the authority fined Empresa Publica de Aguas de Luanda the equivalent of USD 150,000 on 14 July 2026 for inadequate protection of customers' data and failure to notify it.

note: The tally of 15 fined firms and USD 2.5 million is the newspaper's own finding, not a count the authority published.

facts.fact: PTI, citing the authority's map of infringement cases, says the Agencia de Protecao de Dados imposed six fines totalling USD 1.107 million equivalent in 2026 to date, three fines totalling USD 250,000 in 2025 and five totalling USD 600,000 in 2024.
PTI reports the authority fined Standard Bank de Angola USD 150,000 for inadequate security measures after unauthorised access to data of 51 clients.
The Angolan Data Protection Agency (APD) published, under article 53(3) of Law 22/11, its Board of Directors' deliberations 004/2024 and 005/2024 of 19 July 2024, showing the Agency acting.

By deliberations 004/2024 and 005/2024 of 19 July 2024 the APD fined COSAL the equivalent of US$75,000 and ENDE-EP the equivalent of US$225,000 for failing to protect personal data against ransomware attacks of September 2023.
The authority's head signed the statutes of the Lusophone Data Protection Network on 20 March 2025 as a founding member, so Angola's authority is in post.
